captures.what_is_new: The full list of the 78 Portugal-based startups Startup Portugal selected for Road 2 Web Summit 2026, by the article's sectors, each with its city and the article's one-line description (often the company's own words, not checked). By city: Lisbon 41, Porto 11, Braga 9, Aveiro 4, Leiria 2, Azores 2, Madeira 2, and one each from Evora, Torres Vedras, Coimbra, Castelo Branco, Setubal, Sintra and Viseu. By sector: AI and machine learning 14, healthtech and wellness 13, sustainability and cleantech 5, and 21 smaller sectors. They pitch at the summit for the Most Promising Startup award (15,000 euros). Participation rests on this article's account of the selection, not on a Web Summit page.

story_candidates.title: Beyond Lisbon: where Road 2 Web Summit's 78 startups come from
story_candidates.angle: Lisbon has 41 of the 78 startups Startup Portugal selected for Road 2 Web Summit; the other 37 come from Porto (11), Braga (9), Aveiro (4) and ten other places, from the Azores and Madeira to Leiria, Evora and Castelo Branco. A regional tour of who builds what where, with examples from the list, and the 15,000 euro Most Promising Startup award as the reason to watch the pitches.
story_candidates.note: For journalist-portugal. Ready to write now. Conditions: participation rests on Portugal Startup News' account of Startup Portugal's selection, not a Web Summit page, so re-read that article and Startup Portugal's own page the same day and say what the source is; descriptions are not checked; cities as the article gives them; no claim about who will win. Examples in the capture: Braga (ASOagent AI, Savearth, eDynamics, RTBeamTech, Doors App), Porto (Braining, UPWIND Energy, Scooli), Aveiro (ENG8, RFisense, Rexium, Mundo Claro), Azores (Direto AI, Opsivision). Do not give a city for Humanos until its country is checked (see the fact-checker notes).

story_candidates.title: Rehab beyond the clinic: three Portuguese startups at Web Summit
story_candidates.angle: Different technology on the same problem, getting people better outside the clinic: Braining (Porto, AI and virtual reality for stroke rehabilitation), UpSpeech (Lisbon, speech therapy practised at home, with AI-drafted reports), Twin Factory (Lisbon, sensors and digital twins for rehabilitation and athletic performance).
story_candidates.note: NOT READY. Three companies, each known only through one article's one-line description; needs each company's own public page captured (what it does, who it serves) before a writer can verify it. Revisit when the researcher adds them.

S3 says up to 125 Portuguese companies were to be selected; the Portugal Startup News article says 78 were selected. S3 may want an update line with the 78.
Counts per city and sector are the curator's from the 78-entry list; the writer should recount from the article.
